caveats.detail: Independent source-review recommendation by wqp_common_carp_ia_review_r16 under lease-wqp-common-carp-ia-source-review-20260908-r16-1. All 22 leased pairs have supported historical-occurrence witnesses. This is not determination approval, an immutable-run completion, or a claim of 22 compiled gains. MAIN must independently reconstruct and compare these witnesses before admission.

Used Python gzip, zipfile and csv in memory. Verified the r16 bundle hash, every embedded-file length/hash in the r16 and r14 source bundles, original Iowa ZIP CRC, decoded CSV hash, and byte-for-byte equality between the original ZIP member and retained CSV gzip. Parsed 34 Result records and 4164 Station records. The exact leased scope contains 31 Result records across 22 pairs. No missing station joins, ambiguous organization/site joins, exact duplicate Result raw hashes, nonpositive values, or source-date/activity-identifier mismatches were found.

Publisher is EPA National Aquatic Resources Survey (NARS), organization NARS_WQX, delivered through WQP/STORET. The original Iowa HTTP 200 response was retrieved at 2026-09-08T14:51:07.676Z. Provider headers declare 34 results, 34 activities and 32 sites; decoded Result count reconciles to 34. The national Station response was retrieved at 2026-09-08T12:35:04.802Z and reconciles to 4164 sites. The state measurement query is complete only for its retained filters; it does not establish complete county research or exhaustive biological records.

All 22 witnesses are exact Cyprinus carpio, Final, Actual, positive Population Census Count/count, Biological media, Fish/Nekton assemblage, and River/Stream stations. Fourteen use Field Msr/Obs and eight use Sample-Routine. Selected dates span 2008-08-12 through 2014-08-07. Toxicity, detection-condition, qualifier, unidentified-species, tissue-anatomy, laboratory and analytical-method fields are blank. No Provisional, Accepted, Estimated, Frequency Class, zero, composite, length or weight form occurs in the 31 in-scope records. This review does not validate those other forms.

Population Census reports the species count in a sample or collection effort, as documented by the retained EPA WQX glossary. The NRSA manual describes collecting fish in the field, identification by designated fish specialists, species tallies, and correction following identification review. These conditions support historical occurrence from the positive counts without requiring every original photograph or voucher to be reacquired. They do not prove current persistence, establishment, countywide abundance, or absence elsewhere. [EPA 2009 NRSA manual, sections 5.5.3-5.5.5](https://nepis.epa.gov/Exe/ZyPURL.cgi?Dockey=P100AVOF.TXT)

Every in-scope row names Fish Abundance Samp / NCA Standard Fish Sample and includes a generic coastal trawl description, while the project identifies NRSA 2008-2009 or 2013-2014 and equipment says Backpack Electroshock. EPA NRSA manuals describe river field electrofishing and identification/tallying. The 2013-2014 manual also permits secondary backpack electrofishing in shallow parts of non-wadeable reaches. I infer that the coastal description is reused metadata; the exact gear configuration for each activity is not independently resolved. Preserve these original fields and this caveat. Do not describe these Iowa observations as verified coastal trawls or claim complete effort from that description. The field-count occurrence interpretation remains supported. [EPA 2013-2014 non-wadeable manual, sections 10.3.2 and 10.4](https://www.epa.gov/sites/production/files/2016-04/documents/nrsa1314_fom_nonwadeable_version1_20130501.pdf)

County attribution uses the original Station CountryCode US, StateCode 19 and exact CountyCode joined by organization plus monitoring-location identifier. Coordinate checks are diagnostic only. Twenty-one selected points fall inside their stated county in the retained generalized 2025 Census topology. Plymouth 19149 lies approximately 238.3 m outside its coarse polygon at Big Sioux River, longitude -96.60156764, latitude 42.79185309. Both retained station identities explicitly report Iowa/Plymouth. Only those two stations occur within 2 km in the retained national Station source; no conflicting nearby retained county-coded station was found. The topology quantization is approximately 0.003589294 degrees longitude by 0.000859060 degrees latitude, so this river-boundary discrepancy does not independently invalidate the explicit source county. I recommend support with the diagnostic caveat, without reassigning the point or claiming a precise legal boundary. Selected activity/station coordinate differences are below 0.65 m.

Nine additional in-scope records remain corroborating or redundant and are not separate proposed pair gains. No in-scope record requires a biological rejection. Des Moines record index 22 reports fewer than 20 channel widths with more than 500 individuals overall; that is an effort limitation, not a common-carp absence or failed-capture statement. Its positive count is consistent with occurrence, but the primary witness is the independent 2014 activity at index 27. PassCount 2 in repeat visits is not automatically laboratory quality control. Result indexes 18, 25 and 29 are outside the exact lease and are not proposed.

Parsed indexes are zero-based data records excluding the header. Physical end lines are one-based including the header and embedded newlines. Hashes cover exact original CSV record bytes including original line endings. The proposed records are single physical lines, but Station physical line numbers differ from parsed indexes because earlier Station records contain embedded newlines. Original source strings, including numeric values, are preserved.

Attribute EPA NARS as publisher and WQP/STORET as delivery source; retain original query, retrieval, artifact and row identities. The CSV profile does not provide a specific record-license field. This review makes no blanket CC0 or unrestricted-media-rights claim and requires no republication of manual prose or media.

resultFields.SampleCollectionMethod/MethodDescription: Fish and Ephibenthic Invertebrate Collection Fish trawls were conducted at each site to collect fish/shellfish for community structure and abundance estimates, target species for contaminant analyses, and specimens for histopathological examination. Trawls were conducted by using a 16-ft otter trawl and the duration of the trawl will be for 10±2 minutes; replicate (two) trawls will be performed. In open water, the trawl should be conducted in a straight line with the site location near center. The speed over bottom should be approximately 3-4 knots.
